$comment: PromptWheel supply-chain guard-pack. Use via { "extends": ["packs/supply-chain/pack.json"] } in your promptwheel.config.json, or install it with `promptwheel init --preset supply-chain` (which also writes the mandates). Three counts the gate holds: a rise fails the gate unless the change carries a declared reason (`--allow "<reason>"` or a `Promptwheel-Allow:` trailer), which is recorded in the outcome record. gamingCheck is false because these numbers legitimately live in config files (package.json, lockfiles), which the source-only re-run reverts.

metrics.$comment: install-time script entries (preinstall, install, postinstall, prepare, prepublish, prepublishOnly, postpack) across every package.json: the step a supply-chain attack needs inside your repo
metrics.name: lifecycle_scripts

metrics.$comment: dependency entries across every package.json: a new package needs a recorded reason, so every addition leaves an audit line
metrics.name: dependency_entries

metrics.$comment: lockfile entries resolved from outside the npm registry (git, ssh, http, another host's tarball, file:) plus registry entries with no integrity hash: where a package really comes from
metrics.name: lock_nonregistry_sources

metrics.$comment: code run from a floating reference: an action not pinned by SHA, npx or dlx with no exact version, a global install with no exact version, a remote script piped to a shell. Must not rise.
metrics.name: unpinned_execution

metrics.$comment: install protections missing at the repo root: install scripts not disabled, no release-age cooldown. Must not rise.
metrics.name: install_policy_gaps

metrics.$comment: structural items the tree has that promptwheel.lock.json does not. Must not rise.
metrics.name: lock_drift

metrics.$comment: a fingerprint of the resolved dependency tree, compared base to head: a new version under an old name is how a worm arrives. Any change needs a reason.
metrics.name: pins_changed
